Subject: POC/Trial plan & model selection - Acme Corp

Marissa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough this morning — really helpful. I wanted to recap our goals and confirm next steps so we can align our internal stakeholders before we kick off a POC. High-level requirements: 

- Primary use case: multilingual customer support summarization + intent extraction (English, Spanish, French)
- Conversational latency target:  < 300ms p95 for single-request summaries (we understand this is tight)
- Quality target: ROUGE / human eval baseline — summaries should be at least 85% accurate on our test set and preserve named entities
- Cost target: lower total per-1K token cost than our current vendor (we'll share usage profile)

Questions for you:
1) Which open model do you recommend for a 2-week trial considering multilingual needs and cost?
2) Do you have a recommended fallback (smaller/quantized) model for resilience/cost testing?
3) What's the typical timeline and ownership for Redwood to set up a POC (tech onboarding, data ingestion, eval harness)?

Happy to set a kickoff next week. I can invite our engineering lead (Sanjay) if you'd like.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex Johnson
Head of AI Products, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC/Trial plan & model selection - Acme Corp

Alex — great to meet you and thanks for the clear recap. Below is our proposal and suggested next steps for the POC. Attaching a one-page POC-plan and a short requirements summary for your review.

Recommended model for the trial:
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (open, strong instruction-following and cost-effective; good baseline for multilingual prompts)
- Fallback / cost resilience: Llama-2-13B-Chat (quantized variant) or a 7B quantized runtime we host (label: redwood-serve-7b-quant) — we can automatically route to the fallback when latency or quota policies trigger.

Evaluation plan / success criteria:
- Functional: Summaries reach >= 85% accuracy on your provided eval set (we'll set up an A/B between Mistral-7B and the fallback).
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for single-request workloads; we'll run a simulation with your traffic profile to validate.
- Cost: report showing per-token cost across both models and an estimate of monthly spend at your current usage.
- Multilingual: run same eval set in English / Spanish / French. If we see consistent gaps, we can add targeted prompt templates or small-domain adapters.

Timeline & ownership (proposed):
- Kickoff / data handoff: within 3 business days after sign-off (Marissa to own commercial; Ben to own technical onboarding)
- Week 1: technical onboarding, dataset ingestion, baseline runs
- Week 2: run evals, iterate prompts, measure latency/cost
- Week 3-4: optimize routing, run final evaluation, present results and recommendations

Next steps:
1) Confirm kickoff time (we can do Wed/Thu next week).
2) Alex/Sanjay: share a small representative eval set (200-500 examples) and a traffic profile.
3) I'll loop in Ben (solutions engineering) to own the technical setup.

Attachments: POC-plan.pdf (application/pdf), requirements-summary.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

They asked for model recommendations; I proposed Mistral-Instruct-7B as primary and a quantized Llama-2-13B / redwood-serve-7b-quant as fallback.

Can you:

Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC/Trial plan & model selection - Acme Corp

Marissa / Alex — thanks for the context and the materials. Quick answers and next steps from the SE side: 

1) Availability & perf: Mistral-Instruct-7B is available on Hosted with our standard optimized kernels; redwood-serve-7b-quant is available as a fallback (fast, low-cost). Llama-2-13B-Chat (quantized) is also an option but will likely have higher memory/latency, so we typically use it for quality comparisons rather than the primary low-latency path.

2) Routing/fallback recommendation: configure policy based on p95 latency and queue depth — e.g., if p95 > 350ms or queue depth > 8, switch traffic (up to 30%) to the fallback pool for bursts; otherwise route to Mistral-7B. We'll instrument traces so you can see per-request model decisions.

3) Infra estimate for p95 <300ms (single-request): with your expected profile (single request median size ~1.2k tokens, spikes to 5k tokens), we recommend a small Dedicated GPU pool for consistent p95 <300ms in the trial (2x A10-equivalent nodes) or Hosted with autoscale and a higher concurrency setting — I'll send a short cost estimate after we see the traffic profile.

4) Multilingual notes: out-of-the-box Mistral-7B handles EN/ES/FR reasonably with good prompt templates. For persistent gaps (especially entity preservation), we'll add a small domain adapter or curated prompt templates; we can iterate inside Week 2.

Next steps I need from your side (Alex/Sanjay):
- Provide the eval set (200-500 examples) and a 24h traffic profile (typical requests/hour, average tokens).
- Confirm kickoff slot (Thu 10-11am PT works for me).

I'll create a sandbox project, pre-provision the hosted runtime with the two models, and share access.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Phone: +1 (650) 555-0199
